The new Netflix show The Body is garnering backlash for being "blasphemous" and "anti-Christian," with over 110,000 people signing a petition asking Netflix to cancel the show. The Body, which released on the streaming platform on Nov. 11, is a coming-of-age drama by writer, actor and director Quinn Shephard that tells the story of a dance team at a Catholic school.
The petition to cancel the coming-of-age drama has reached over 110,000 signatures so far
The new Netflix show The Body is taking heat for being "blasphemous" and "anti-Christian," with more than 110,000 people signing a petition calling on the streaming giant to cancel the show.
The Body, which released on Netflix on Nov. 11, is a coming-of-age drama by writer, actor and director Quinn Shephard. It tells the story of a dance team at a Catholic school.

In the show, the girls perform a mock satanic ritual at a Halloween party, pretending to offer one of their classmates as a virgin sacrifice. Afterward, the girls begin having prophetic visions, sparking hysteria in their town.
The petition on CitizenGO calls it: "A blasphemous anti-Christian series featuring satanic ritual."
"Parents cannot screen every show teens press play on. Netflix is counting on that," it says.
As of publication, the eight-episode series is third in Netflix Canada's top 10. According to Variety, it drew 5.1 million views in its first five days in the U.S.

The petition was launched before the show's premiere and initially called on Netflix not to release it. As of Nov. 19, just over a week after the show was released, it had received more than 118,000 signatures.
The petition also criticized Netflix's marketing campaign for posting photos portraying the show's characters as saints.
Not the first program protested

The petition also criticizes previous Netflix releases, including The First Temptation of Christ — a Brazilian comedy released in 2019 — for mocking Jesus. It also mentions the 2020 French drama Cuties, saying it "sexualized eleven-year-old girls."
Despite protests, streaming platforms rarely respond by removing content from their libraries.

In 2019, more than 20,000 people signed a petition to cancel the series Good Omens, claiming it mocked God and normalized Satanism. However, protesters mistakenly addressed their petition to Netflix rather than Amazon, which produced the series. Good Omens went on to have a second and third season.

In 2021, about 100 Netflix employees staged a protest outside the company's headquarters in Los Angeles over Dave Chappelle's comedy special, The Closer. Protesters said the special was transphobic. Netflix kept the special available on its platform.

The animated sitcom South Park has also faced numerous controversies involving various groups, including Christians, Muslims, Mormons and the Trump administration. The series is now in its 29th season.
CBC reached out to Netflix for comment on the petition but did not receive a response before publication. Netflix has yet to confirm whether the series will be renewed for a second season.
